correctness.rationale: Exact formulas for five Legendre quotients are from a tame (Z/2)^4 decomposition. The degree-eight p17 Hasse polynomial factors into four separable irreducible quadratics, and all its roots are explicitly enumerated over F289. Transitive S5 relabeling reduces any two supersingularity conditions to 56 ordered distinct Hasse-root pairs; exact field arithmetic checks 44 with multiplicity 2 and 12 with multiplicity 5 and no others. S5 orbit enumeration proves the 12 form one orbit. Local coordinate and simple-root arguments show transversality, and counting over extensions gives the displayed formulas. The 2-primary kernel of the quotient-product isogeny preserves 17-divisible groups; thus the a-number and p-rank are valid. The standalone verifier reproduces the full F289 82082-parameter census and all reported certificate counts. Limits: marked smooth parameters only.

originality.rationale: The earlier quotient isogeny and the special five-isomorphic-elliptic golden-ratio configuration (Carvacho–Hidalgo–Quispe, Theorem 5.1 and §5.2), Deuring–Hasse root criteria (Auer–Top, §3), and later superspecial genus-five existence (Ohashi, Theorem 1.2) are prior art. The assessed contribution is the full characteristic-17 incidence of all five supersingularity divisors, complete absence of triple-only and quadruple-only strata, unique 12-point fivefold S5 orbit, and exact rational-parameter counts for all finite extensions. Verified primary texts and searched records provide no covering table. Unindexed or earlier unpublished calculations remain a priority risk.
residual_risks: The golden-ratio superspecial example and its label orbit are very close to known 2015 complex all-isomorphic quotient geometry; the numerical novelty claim is confined to the global exhaustive incidence classification and all-extension distribution.

value.rationale: The geometric coincidence of all five elliptic-quotient supersingularity divisors at exactly twelve marked points, and the absence of exact three- or four-divisor intersections anywhere, is a natural complete incidence classification in a two-dimensional moduli family, not a chosen arbitrary slice. It yields a previously unreported gap in possible geometric Jacobian p-ranks and exact all-extension stratum counts. Existence of the golden-ratio superspecial example is acknowledged as prior; the more demanding exhaustive classification and its arithmetic implications constitute the mathematically motivated contribution.
